gaps.sentence: I haven't got ___ cash on me — I'll pay by card.
gaps.explanation: 'Any' is the normal quantifier in negative sentences; 'haven't got no cash' would be a double negative.

gaps.sentence: The new model has ___ moving parts, so it breaks down less often.
gaps.explanation: 'Fewer moving parts' is correct because 'parts' is countable and plural.

gaps.sentence: This cup is cracked — could I have ___ one?
gaps.explanation: 'Another one' means one more, unspecified; 'the other one' would mean a specific second cup.

gaps.sentence: She has two children. One lives in Leeds, and ___ lives in York.
gaps.hint: one of a pair of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... the other ...' is the pattern for exactly two; 'another' would imply more than two.
'Too cold to swim' means the temperature prevents swimming; 'enough' would follow the adjective.

gaps.sentence: ___ the information you gave was correct.
gaps.explanation: 'All the information' is correct; 'none/neither' would need 'of' and 'both' requires two separate countable items.

gaps.hint: general statement without 'the' — 'people' has no article
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' means people in general; 'most of' needs 'the' (most of the people).

gaps.hint: the defined remainder of a known group
gaps.explanation: 'The others' refers to the specific remaining students; 'the other' is singular.
